SP-424 The Voyage of Mariner 10, ch. 5 (Venus Bound)
SP-424 The Voyage of Mariner 10, ch. 7 (Mercury, Moonlike and Earthlike)
Cape Canaveral Complex 36B, 1973-11-03 05:45 UTC (12:45 a.m. EST). Atlas/Centaur No. 34 sends Mariner 10 first into a 188 km parking orbit, then onto a trajectory to Venus.
13 November 1973 (PST), sequence completed 5:08 p.m. PST = 01:08 UTC on 14 November. A 19.9-second burn of about 7.8 m/s (planned) aims the probe at the Venus gravity-assist point.
1974-01-21 19:14 UTC. Rolling started 11:50 a.m. PDT; 24 min later the engine fires for 3.8 s, about 1.3 m/s, refining the Venus flyby and the later arrival at Mercury.
1974-02-05 17:01 UT. Closest approach 5,768 km; the first spacecraft to use one planet's gravity to reach another bends Mariner 10 toward Mercury and returns the first close-up Venus images.
1974-03-16 11:54 UTC. A 51-second burn of 17.8 m/s directly away from the Sun moves the first Mercury flyby to the dark side of the planet and sets up a return in six months.
1974-03-29 20:46 UT. Closest approach about 704 km above the night side; the first spacecraft to reach Mercury. SP-424 gives 1:46 p.m. PDT.
First Mercury flyby; first dual-planet flyby; first gravity-assist mission

First spacecraft to visit Mercury, first to fly past two planets, and first to use a gravity assist to reach its destination. Launched 1973-11-03 05:45 UTC from Cape Canaveral LC-36B on Atlas SLV-3D Centaur AC-34. Mariner 10 swung past Venus on 1974-02-05 (5768 km closest approach, first UV cloud-belt imaging of Venus) using the encounter to drop its perihelion into Mercury's orbital realm — the first use of one planet's gravity to reach another. Made three Mercury flybys: 1974-03-29 (703 km), 1974-09-21 (48069 km), and 1975-03-16 (327 km). Imaged ~45% of Mercury's surface — the only resolved imagery available until MESSENGER (2008-2015). Discovered Mercury's intrinsic magnetic field and thin helium exosphere. Solar-array temperature management was an open mission engineering problem: project scientists tilted the panels and rolled the spacecraft to keep them under 115°C. Mission ended 1975-03-24 when attitude-control nitrogen propellant was depleted; spacecraft is presumed to be in heliocentric orbit, periodically passing Mercury.
Atlas SLV-3D Centaur AC-34 from CCAFS LC-36B 1973-11-03 05:45 UTC.
